subject: SIG/CAIQ request: 3P snapshot + attestation timeline
messages:
From: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@acmehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>; Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ request: 3P snapshot + attestation timeline

Hi David / team,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As part of ACME's procurement and security review, our InfoSec team needs a current SIG/CAIQ bundle plus a third-party (subprocessor) snapshot that lists providers, purpose, location (jurisdiction), and KMS ownership. We need the following items to progress the security review: 

- Completed SIG questionnaire or CAIQ export (PDF preferred)
- A CSV snapshot of all subprocessors with columns: name, service, region, data access scope, KMS owner (redwood/third party), and SOC2/ISO status
- Any SOC 2 or other attestation PDFs you can share
- Short note on how you handle onshore vs. offshore subprocessors and any planned changes in the next 90 days

Our timeline is tight: can you provide the artifacts by EOD Thursday 2025-07-31? If not, please propose an alternate timeline and any quick mitigations we can present to procurement.

If there are parts that must go through your legal or compliance team (e.g., redlines, DSAs), please flag those separately.

Appreciate it — Claire

--
Claire Bennett
Senior Security Engineer, ACME Health
claire.bennett@acmehealth.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ request: 3P snapshot + attestation timeline

Claire — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick clarifications so we can prioritize: 

1) For KMS ownership column: do you want the effective owner for runtime keys (who holds customer-encrypted keys) or the owner of platform service keys? We can provide both but prefer to confirm which you need for procurement.
2) For SOC2 status: listing of whether each subprocessor is covered by Redwood's SOC2 or the subprocessor's own SOC2 is fine; we'll include both where applicable.
3) Is a CAIQ export fine in lieu of a completed SIG questionnaire, or do you require the standard SIG spreadsheet?

Tentative plan: Marissa will assemble the subprocessor snapshot and SOC2 artifacts; Jonas will attach the CAIQ export. If you need a signed attestation, we can surface that via our legal team (DocuSign).

I'll push to get the initial bundle by tomorrow EOD. If that's still insufficient, we'll propose a staged delivery (CSV + CAIQ first, followed by signed attestation).

-David

--
David Kim
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ request: SIG export + subprocessor snapshot (attachments)

Claire — attaching the initial artifacts per David's note. See the files included below (attachments).

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_subprocessor_snapshot_20250731.csv (csv) — columns: name | service | region | data_scope | kms_owner | soc2_status | notes
- redwood_sig_answers_v1.pdf (pdf) — CAIQ export + notes for items we commonly see questions on

Key callouts inside the CSV:
- "ephemeral-keys" provider (CloudKeyOps) has runtime KMS ownership; data access is limited to ephemeral caching and is scoped to non-PII workloads
- Data-storage providers in eu-west-1 are operated by our Dedicated partners; KMS ownership is with Redwood for customer-managed keys where requested (indicated in kms_owner column)
- A small set of analytics vendors are US-based contractors with SOC2 Type II in process (we've noted estimated completion dates)

We do not expect material changes to the roster in the next 30 days; there is a planned evaluation of an on-prem inference partner in Q4 which we flagged in the CSV notes.

Links: evidence bundle and working folder -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-evidence

Requested next steps: 
- Claire: confirm whether the CAIQ export + CSV meet your team's needs for the procurement checkpoint.
- If ACME needs a signed attestation (DocuSign), we'll route to legal — estimated turnaround 3 business days once the request is formalized.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Aug 2025 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ request: SIG export + subprocessor snapshot (attachments)

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. The CSV and CAIQ export cover 90% of the checklist. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/security: 

- Please add a one-line attestation (signed) that the snapshot is complete as of 2025-07-31 and that no offshored subprocessors have access to unencrypted customer PII.
- For the analytics vendors that are "SOC2 in process," please attach any interim evidence (e.g., SOC2 readiness report, scope doc) if available.

Procurement is prepared to accept a staged delivery (CSV + CAIQ first, attestation to follow). We'll accept the DocuSign attestation and expect legal to coordinate on the wording.

I'll queue the DocuSign envelope when you send the attestation request link — thanks for the rapid turnaround.
